options: Stacks rows from one DataFrame directly beneath another — rows top to bottom, the opposite of a join's side-by-side columns
Combines columns from two DataFrames side by side, like a join

questions.q: How does union() match up columns between the two DataFrames?

questions.explain: If two files have columns in a different order, union() silently mixes up the data instead of raising an error.

questions.q: What real risk does position-based matching create in union()?

The union() call always raises an error if column order differs

questions.q: How does unionByName() avoid the silent-swap risk of plain union()?
options: It looks up each column by its actual name instead of its position in the schema
It ignores all columns except the first one
It automatically renames every column before combining
It has the exact same risk as union() with no real difference
questions.explain: Unless there's a specific reason not to, unionByName() is the safer default for combining real-world files.
